words.name: anchi-piri
words.gloss: Obsidian and a cut: the word carries the tool and the wound, and no word for ink.

words.name: batok
words.gloss: From Proto-Austronesian *beCik, tattoo, with relatives *patik, mottled, and *burik, speckled — the word for a pattern, applied to skin, cloth and pot alike.

words.name: deq
words.gloss: From Syriac *dyoqo*, puncturing. A male tattooist is *deqqak*, a female one *deqqake*.

words.name: godna
words.gloss: To prick. The noun for the tattoo and the verb for the needle are the same word.

words.name: hajichi
words.gloss: Needle-strike. Written with the characters for needle and thrust.

words.name: htoe kwin
words.gloss: *Htoe* is to prick or pierce; *kwin* is a ring or an enclosure. The name describes the framed rings the figures sit in.

words.name: irezumi
words.gloss: Inserting ink. The word names the material and the direction of travel, and nothing about the hand.

words.name: kakiniq
words.gloss: From the Proto-Inuit-Yupik root *kaki-, to pierce or prick — the same root across Iñupiaq, Inuktitut, West Greenlandic and Tunumiit.

words.name: lao phung dam
words.gloss: "Black-bellied Lao" — a central Thai name for the tattooed northerner, applied from outside and carrying a view with it.

words.name: ming
words.gloss: The Chin word for the facial marks. Banned by name in the 1960s.

words.name: moko
words.gloss: *Tā* is to strike; *moko* is the design itself. The verb in the name is the mallet, not the point.

words.name: ptasan
words.gloss: Related to the Atayal word for writing and marking — the face as a written surface.

words.name: sak kha lai
words.gloss: To prick the legs in patterns — the verb, the body part and the word for pattern, in that order. No separate noun for the tattoo is needed.

words.name: sak
words.gloss: To prick. The Khmer root *cɔkʔ* means the same, and the Khmer dictionary keeps it native rather than borrowed.

words.name: sicanje
words.gloss: Pricking. Colloquially also *bocanje* and *bockanje*, which mean the same and sound like it.

words.name: tatau
words.gloss: The Polynesian word English borrowed. Cook's crew wrote it down in 1769 and it displaced every English word for the practice.

words.name: tua mueang
words.gloss: The northern letters — Tai Tham script, the script of the region's manuscripts and of the yant that go on northern skin. Khom is the central convention, not the northern one.

words.name: veiqia
words.gloss: The practice and the marks, in one word — and a tattooist is a *dauveiqia*, one who does veiqia.
